backbone: Encode prefixes as a Gaussian coefficient body; uniform Gaussian-survival and matrix-variation estimates give small diagonal Dirichlet energy, and a lifted-symmetrization proposition then yields signs keeping all states bounded.
quote: The body of coefficients for which every state is bounded will provide the simultaneous control of all prefixes.

backbone: Explicitly construct a multiscale doubling subset of l2; a lexicographic extremal-derivative energy estimate plus crossings forces a packing contradiction for any bi-Lipschitz map into R^k.
quote: There is a fixed subset $S$ of real $\ell_2$, equipped with its induced Hilbert distance, whose doubling constant is at most $76800$ and which admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into $\R^k$

backbone: Recursively construct binary word families over prime-product groups with cheap steps and separated shifts; a Fourier/cut displacement inequality forces large l1 distortion; a substring-histogram embedding gives the upper bound.
quote: The construction below reaches the scale of the Ostrovsky--Rabani exponent.

backbone: Subdivide Bang's two-cylinder cover into narrow tilted angular sectors, verify coverage of the tetrahedron, and expand the total base area to show it drops below half.
quote: We construct a counterexample with compact triangular bases.

backbone: Prove the sharp entropy bound for log-concave densities via Gaussian Brenier transport and a chaos decomposition of the entropy deficit (scalar estimates certified rationally), then deduce the simplex inequality.
quote: The proof proceeds through differential entropy.

backbone: Explicit PCP-style reduction from Hastad's parity gap through a latent matrix-shortcode test; completeness by construction, soundness by Fourier decoding using the Grassmann-expansion inverse theorem plus repetition.
quote: For every fixed \(\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2)\), we give a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) to Unique Games over a fixed finite alphabet

backbone: Construct an explicit deterministic log-space compiler: a recursive correction-and-copy hierarchy approximates acceptance probabilities, with a telescoping space budget along the recursion and error estimates throughout.

backbone: Quantitative discount reduction to discounted monotone maps, then an explicit recursive simultaneous-labeling procedure on witnesses, whose correctness is proved by induction on rank, yielding an exact quasipolynomial decision.
quote: There is a terminating deterministic procedure $\cL(A,D,a,b)$, using exact evaluations of $\lfloor F(t)\rfloor$ for $t\in\Z^n$ and integer and rational arithmetic

backbone: Explicit reduction from a perfect-completeness repeated PCP game through a tree of function spaces with a one-bit test; soundness decodes strategies via Grassmann-expansion inverse shortcode estimates.
quote: there are an integer $q=q(\delta)\ge2$ and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from $3$-SAT to 2-to-1 games with alphabets $[2q]$ and $[q]$

backbone: Explicit graph reduction from perfect-completeness Label Cover; a large independent set is decoded to bounded label lists, aligned via minimax and Ramsey, then a coefficient test gives soundness.
quote: there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm $R_\delta$ that maps each explicitly encoded Boolean $3$-CNF formula $\phi$ to a nonempty finite simple undirected unweighted graph $G_\phi$

backbone: Via Strassen's spectral duality, bound every tensor character on matrix multiplication: explicit degenerations give concavity and tripling for a polynomial-multiplication profile, whose discrete growth forces t<=3/4.
quote: The present proof combines explicit tensor degenerations with the spectral viewpoint. It derives inequalities for character values on polynomial multiplication, then uses their discrete growth to bound the values on matrix multiplication.

backbone: Project the permanent to a smooth form of large degree and dimension (characteristic-two adjugate/conductor analysis), then a polar-intersection count lower-bounds border determinantal complexity of smooth forms.
quote: Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth-border} proves the version needed here, including persistence of finitely many simple polar intersections in one sufficiently close determinant under an arbitrary coefficientwise approximation.

backbone: Explicit multitape algorithm: finite linear networks with a rank saving give faster address-chunk interchange and synthetic butterfly layers, recursively lowering the FFT-based multiplication cost below n log n.
quote: We construct two fixed linear networks that exchange two banks of values while restoring every auxiliary value.

backbone: For each known request law build a policy on a posterior-driven HST (tree allocation, partitions, rounding) with O(log^2 k) cost; finite minimax and product compactness yield one oblivious policy.
quote: The distributional estimates are converted into a single policy by finite minimax and product compactness.

backbone: Explicit randomized rule for fixed hidden weights (maximum branch plus layered nested flats from sampled density expansions and guards); bound rank for every order, then couple to one-sample model.
quote: We construct the rule of Proposition~\ref{prop:hidden} for a fixed hidden weight vector.

backbone: Explicit polynomial-evaluation language whose probabilistically good slices have low correlation with bounded-width CNFs under restrictions; summing middle gates of a small OR-AND-OR circuit contradicts acceptance density.
quote: We construct a language with a data block and parameter blocks.

backbone: Explicit FPRAS: marked-edge subdivisions with vertex scaling; a two-coordinate Dirichlet energy inequality gives a rapidly mixing sampler, and an annealing schedule converts samples into the count.

backbone: Explicit annealing MCMC algorithm on weighted port profiles; integer signature (Lorentzian-type) inequalities give log-concavity and transport bounds, hence Poincare/mixing estimates and polynomial-cost approximate counting.
quote: There is a single uniform randomized algorithm which, for every input described above, outputs a nonnegative rational $\widehat Z$ satisfying

backbone: Explicit sampler: pad large margins, run a Markov chain on small-cell states whose mixing follows from signature-based transport variance bounds, then apply residual-mixture exact correction.
quote: We give an exact uniform sampler for nonnegative integer contingency tables with arbitrary prescribed margins.

backbone: Explicit matrix tuple from independent word series under a multiplicative shift; formulas give finite shift systems whose order-of-vanishing bound ensures nonvanishing after truncation and descent to the prime field.
quote: We construct a single matrix substitution that detects every nonzero size-s division-free noncommutative formula in n variables over every field of a given positive characteristic.

backbone: Explicit reduction from a bit-test PCP system with an explicit pencil of directions to unit-demand graphs; sparse cuts are decoded to valuations via an analytic score gap, giving soundness.
quote: For every fixed real constant $C>1$, there is a polynomial-time reduction from $3$CNF satisfiability to finite undirected graphs with nonnegative rational capacities and exactly unit demands

backbone: Explicit vertex-cover-to-bin-packing reduction built on two competing quota trees; covers give B-bin packings, the LP equals B, and near-optimal packings yield small covers.
quote: We disprove the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture for bin packing by constructing instances with arbitrarily large additive gaps between the configuration-LP value and the integral optimum.

backbone: Prove a local entropy-production (joining) inequality via a three-point optimizer, capacities and thinning, lift it by induction on cube dimension, and integrate along the noise semigroup.
quote: The proof combines an explicit three-point optimizer for the local joining problem, two entropy capacities, and a common-output thinning inequality, followed by dimension induction and integration along the noise semigroup.

backbone: Explicit randomized algorithm: phases with structural matching operations and blossom contraction, priced logarithmic steps on a forest backend, and a routing sparsifier, analysed recursively for almost-linear time.
quote: There are a single uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm, fixed constants $c_0\ge2$ and $C\ge1$, and a nonincreasing function $\eta:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$

backbone: Explicit algorithm over a hierarchical interval tree: precision-sampled seed estimates, then repeated entropy-regularized refinement passes with regret bounds giving a (1+eps) estimate in almost-linear time.

backbone: Build, by induction over scales, pairs of distinct strings whose trace laws stay close (common mass, smoothing, likelihood cancellation), then transfer to complete traces for the sample lower bound.
quote: The proof is by induction. Section~\ref{sec:initial} supplies level zero. Proposition~\ref{prop:block} constructs the next level

backbone: Show every feasible schedule admits a recursive interval hierarchy with bounded global descriptions; a dynamic program over the polynomially many described sets then finds an optimal schedule.
quote: The proof reorganizes feasible schedules into intervals whose job sets have descriptions of bounded size. A dynamic program searches a family containing polynomially many such descriptions.

backbone: Explicit LP-based algorithm: prepare openings, tapered iterative dependent rounding analysed by a certified finite drift inequality, derandomize, then remove the additive surplus via Li-Svensson.
quote: Our approach first permits a constant additive surplus, makes that approximation deterministic, and then removes the surplus using an established reduction.

backbone: Assume a small PSD factorization of the shifted slack matrix; Fourier smoothing over product averages converts it into low-degree squares, which a separating functional on an expanding parity system contradicts.
quote: This is the step that lets the separating functional contradict the factorization.

backbone: A one-sided coupling inequality for equal-law variables combined with a weighted Fourier grading operator whose anticommutator recovers sensitive edges directly bounds total influence by 8d sqrt(n).
quote: The proof separates a probability estimate from a finite-dimensional operator construction.

backbone: Forced occurrence counts give a balanced substring graph of cost at most OPT; periodic-layer processing connects it with closed walks costing at most W; output an Euler tour.
quote: If its support is connected and visits the empty word and every required string, an Euler tour spells a common superstring whose length is its up-edge cost.
